subject: Dedicated throughput guarantees — measurement approach, penalties, and sizing
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@skyline-analytics.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@skyline-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Throughput guarantee ask for Dedicated commit

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re evaluating a reserved GPU pool with Redwood and need to lock in throughput guarantees for our MLP-based summarization pipeline. High level ask: a committed tokens/sec guarantee and a latency SLO at p95.

Questions we need answered before procurement:
- How do you measure tokens/sec (synthetic load vs production sampling)?
- What measurement window do you use (1m, 5m, 15m)?
- How do you handle KV cache warmup and prefix caching in the benchmark?
- If you miss the guarantee, what credits/offsets do you provide and how are they calculated?

We’d like a baseline proposal by EOD Thursday so procurement can budget. Attaching a short doc with our expected QPS and payload sizes.

Cheers,
Aisha Khan
Head of ML Platforms
Skyline Analytics

Attachment: skyline_payload_samples.csv (referenced in their doc)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@skyline-analytics.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantee ask for Dedicated commit

Aisha — thanks for the clear list. I’ve looped in Vanessa (capacity/product) and Ben (commercial). We’ll do a short internal check and come back with a concrete measurement approach and a preliminary sizing + discount path.

Quick notes: we typically certify throughput using a combination of synthetic driver runs (to validate tokens/sec ceilings) and a small in-region production sampling run (to account for real prompt distributions and KV cache behavior). The SLA window we propose for committed guarantees is a 15-minute sustained throughput measured at the model endpoint at the customer’s committed capacity. Latency SLOs at p95 are measured over the same window.

We’ll follow up with:
- exact test harness we’ll run (script + config)
- how KV cache/prefix caching is accounted for
- sizing in GPUs for their requested sustained TPS/tokens/sec 
- a draft of the credit calculation for shortfalls

Jonas
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Jan 2028 14:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: proposed test plan + sizing for Skyline

Team — reading Aisha’s attachment and Skyline’s expected mix: 60% short summaries (~150 tokens output, 1.2k input tokens avg) and 40% long extracts (~1k output, 2.5k input). They want a committed 250k tokens/sec at p95 with p95 latency <= 350ms.

Proposed approach:
1) Synthetic ceiling run: stress driver to measure max tokens/sec for the model profile (our vetted Llama-variant quantized to 4-bit) with KV cache disabled and then with warmed KV cache. This gives ceiling and cache uplift factor.
2) Production sampling run: deploy a short-lived dedicated pool in their region (4 GPUs initially) and run replay of a 30-minute sampled payload (their real request distribution) to measure sustained tokens/sec and p95 latency. We recommend a 15-minute acceptance window for contractual measurement; operational monitoring continues at 5-minute granularity.
3) Pass/fail: pass if sustained tokens/sec >= committed rate and p95 latency <= target across the 15-minute window. If fail, we pay a pro-rated credit equal to (% shortfall) * monthly commit value, applied as account credit. Example: 10% shortfall over acceptance window => 10% of that period’s proportionate invoice credited.

Sizing: based on our internal perf matrix, target sustained 250k tokens/sec (their mix) maps to ~10x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (approx 4x per GPU for seq-lengthed workload) — recommend proposing an initial reserved pool of 12 GPUs to give headroom + autoscale burst.

Discount posture: for a 12 GPU / 12 month commit we can offer a 20% commit discount; 24-month -> 28%. Ben, please confirm commercial lever. Laura — flag any legal concerns about credit wording (calculation fairness, auditability).

Vanessa
Sr PM, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Attachment (internal): redwood-throughput-test-plan.xlsx

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@skyline-analytics.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantee ask for Dedicated commit

Aisha — thanks for the note and the payload sketch. We’re aligned on the measurement approach Vanessa outlined. A few commercial clarifications:

- Commit sizing: we’ll propose a 12 GPU reserved pool as Vanessa suggested. That’s the commit we’d price and discount against.
- Measurement window: acceptance testing will be billed as standard usage during the test but will not count toward the committed quota for the first 72 hours post-commissioning.
- Credits: If we fail monthly SLA (measured on a rolling 15-minute window), credits will be calculated as: max(0, (CommittedRate - ObservedRate)/CommittedRate) * MonthlyCommitFee * (MinutesAffected / TotalMinutesInMonth). We’ll cap credits at 50% of monthly fee.
- Auditability: we’ll publish the test harness and raw run logs to a shared S3 link and provide a daily CSV with sampled latencies/tokens to their procurement/legal for three months post-launch.

As for discounts: 12x12 -> 20% discount, 12x24 -> 26% discount (Ben note: we tightened 24-month slightly to preserve margin). We can also add a 3% market-penetration incentive if they prepay Q1 of 2028.

If that sounds acceptable, we can convert the draft SLA into the redlines doc and send to your procurement team for review.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales (Dedicated)
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@skyline-analytics.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@skyline-analytics.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 11:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantee ask for Dedicated commit

Ben/Team — thanks. A few clarifying replies from procurement and infra:
- Measurement transparency is critical. We need raw logs and the exact driver config you run. Is the synthetic driver open or black-box?
- Credits cap at 50% is ok but we want a minimum remediation SLA (e.g., engineering remediation plan within 24 hours of sustained failures >10%).
- Sizing: procurement prefers an initial 10 GPU commit (to match budget) but requires ability to burst to 14 for peak monthly windows.

Also attached are our procurement terms; we’ll mark legal redlines inline. Please include Laura from Redwood legal in the next round — we’ll expect negotiated language around measurement and dispute resolution.

Regards,
Aisha

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@skyline-analytics.com>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 16:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantee ask for Dedicated commit

Aisha — copying final positions from our side and proposed contract language snippets for the SLA test and credits.

Summary of agreed measurement methodology (proposed contractual wording):
1) Measurement Metric: "Sustained token throughput" measured as tokens/sec aggregated at the model endpoint. Tokens computed by Redwood tokenization using the model's tokenizer at time of measurement.
2) Acceptance Window: a rolling 15-minute sustained window. A pass requires observed tokens/sec >= CommittedRate and p95 latency <= CommittedLatency across that 15-minute window.
3) Test Harness: Redwood will publish the synthetic driver (open binaries + config) and will provide the exact driver config and raw logs used for certification to Skyline via a signed S3 link. The driver will support an option to replay customer-sampled requests for the production sampling run.
4) KV cache handling: acceptance will be executed twice during certification — (a) cold-cache run (cache disabled) and (b) warmed-cache run (cache warmed by a 10-minute warmup replay). The contractual guarantee will be based on warmed-cache results; cold-cache metrics will be documented for transparency.
5) Credits: if monthly rolling measurements show any 15-minute window where observed throughput < CommittedRate, Redwood will calculate credits as: ((CommittedRate - ObservedRate)/CommittedRate) * MonthlyCommitFee * (MinutesAffected / TotalMinutesInMonth), capped at 50% monthly fee. Engineering remediation plan triggered for aggregate shortfall >10% in a calendar week with a commitment to present a remediation timeline within 24 hours.

We will prepare a redlines-ready doc (draft-sla-redlines-v2.docx) and send it over; happy to accept inline comments. If Skyline is ok with 10 GPU initial commit with burst to 14 and 12-month term at 20% discount, we can issue an initial commercial term sheet.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal (Commercial Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: draft-sla-redlines-v2.docx
